title: A failed generation strands its lane until the app restarts
description: commandExecutor registers a job in generationStore (commandExecutor.js:1293) and then has TWELVE early-return paths that call exec.onError and return WITHOUT settling it: cancelled_before_dispatch, operation_not_installed, arch_weight_missing, model_missing, required_media_slot_empty, model_not_local, the workflow fetch, the trimmed-video prep, and the surrounding catches. _laneBusy(lane) in generationService derives from generationStore.getSnapshot().running, which filters on !TERMINAL_PHASES.has(phase), so a registered-but-never-settled job keeps that lane busy FOREVER and _dispatchNextCue skips it on every pass. The cue then never drains. Symptom is a card stuck on QUEUED, the CUE counter climbing, the engine /queue EMPTY and nothing in app.log - it reads as a dead app or a dead button, not as a failed generation, and only an app restart or renderer reload clears it. Seen live 2026-08-06 during MPI-452: a workflow fetch 404 stranded the local lane, and the next Finish sat queued behind a job that had already errored. NOT downloads-related - that is a separate subsystem. Root fix is one helper that settles PHASES.ERROR before returning, replacing all twelve bare exec.onError calls; do not spot-fix the one path that was hit. cancelled_before_dispatch is the only one that even advances the phase, and it advances rather than settles.
acceptance: Every early-return error path between generationStore.register and the first settle marks the job terminal, so the lane frees
One shared helper does it - not twelve hand-edited call sites, and not only the path that was reported
A test proves a lane recovers after a failed dispatch: enqueue a job that errors before submit, then confirm the NEXT job on that lane still dispatches
The user-visible failure is surfaced too - a stranded QUEUED card with no error is the reported symptom, so the toast/dialog must say what failed
